question: Which of the following is the unified inundation forecasting system launched by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in July 2025 that provides two‑days advance inundation forecasts up to village level in the form of flood‑inundation maps and water‑level predictions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C‑FLOOD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **C‑FLOOD** is a unified inundation forecasting system launched by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** in **July 2025**.
 
• The system provides **two-day advance flood inundation forecasts** at the village level, allowing for better preparedness and disaster management.
 
• It generates **flood-inundation maps** and **water-level predictions**, which are critical for local authorities and communities to plan evacuation and relief operations.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's focus on leveraging **technology and data analytics** to mitigate the impact of floods, which annually affect millions across India.
 
• This forecasting system integrates data from multiple sources, including weather forecasts, hydrological models, and satellite imagery, to provide accurate and actionable insights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Flood Forecasting:**

 
 
• Flooding affects over **75 lakh hectares** of land annually in India, causing significant economic losses and affecting livelihoods.
 
• Forecasting systems like C‑FLOOD reduce the loss of life and property by enabling timely evacuation and resource allocation.
 
 
 
• **Technology Used in C‑FLOOD:**
 
 
• Incorporates **hydrological and hydraulic models** to simulate flood scenarios.
 
• Utilizes **satellite data** for real-time monitoring of water levels and rainfall patterns.
 
• Relies on **machine learning algorithms** to improve the accuracy of predictions over time.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti's Role:**
 
 
• The Ministry oversees water resource management, including flood control and forecasting.
 
• It collaborates with agencies such as the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and **Central Water Commission (CWC)** for data sharing and analysis.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Systems:**
 
 
• Unlike older systems, C‑FLOOD provides **granular, village-level data**, making it more effective for localized disaster management.
 
• It offers forecasts up to **48 hours in advance**, which is a significant improvement over earlier models that provided shorter lead times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Flood Forecasting:**

 
 
• Limited availability of high-resolution data in remote areas.
 
• Need for inter-agency coordination to ensure timely dissemination of forecasts.
 
• Improving community awareness and response mechanisms to maximize the utility of forecasts.
 
 
 
• **Other Flood Management Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• The **National Flood Forecasting and Warning Network** run by the Central Water Commission.
 
• Deployment of **Automatic Rain Gauges (ARGs)** and **Telemetry Systems** for real-time data collection.
 
• State-level initiatives such as flood zoning and embankment construction.
